memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said: 'I am making a covenant with you. Before all your people I will do wonders never before done in any nation in all the world. The people you live among will see how awesome is the work that I, the Lord, will do for you.'" - Exod 34:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"I am making a covenant with you." God initiates. God binds Himself. Israel does not negotiate terms or earn a place at the table.

Every covenant in Scripture works this way. God comes to Noah, to Abraham, to David — always moving first toward people who had done nothing to deserve it. Grace is always God's first move.

Notice also who is meant to see: "the people you live among." God's work in Israel was never meant to stay private. The surrounding nations were supposed to look and wonder. Israel was blessed to be a light.

The same holds for us. God does not renew and restore us so we can enjoy it quietly. Jesus said to let our light shine before others, so that they may see our good deeds and glorify our Father in heaven (Matt 5:16). The wonder is meant to be visible.

But be careful here — this promise of "wonders never before done" was spoken to Israel at a specific point in redemptive history, and it was fulfilled in the conquest and the nation's story. It is not a guarantee of spectacular experiences for us. What we can say with full confidence is that the God who acts is unchanged, and His greatest wonder has already occurred: a crucified man walked out of a tomb.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God moved toward you before you moved toward Him?
2. Who is watching your life and what are they seeing?
3. Do you live as though God's work in you is meant to be seen?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You made the first move toward me. Let Your work in my life be visible to those around me, for Your glory. Amen.
